introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0565 Human Biology 1, June 2026, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer for each question. Duration: one and a half hours.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one best answer, A, B, C or D. Questions 8 and 14 are each printed in two alternative versions (OR) that have the same answer. For questions 31 to 34, ONE OR MORE of the responses are correct: choose A if 1, 2 and 3 are all correct; B if 1 and 2 are correct; C if 2 and 3 are correct; D if 1 only is correct.

figures.legende: Outline of the human body showing four endocrine glands numbered 1 (head, pituitary), 2 (neck, thyroid), 3 (top of the kidney, adrenal) and 4 (pelvis, gonad) (Question 8).
Longitudinal section through the human heart with parts numbered 1 to 4; part 2 is the septum; credit: Roland Super, Human Biology Study Guide (Question 14).

incertitudes: Sujet lu sur un scan sans couche texte, 6 pages (couverture + 5 pages de questions) : les 50 questions sont presentes et lisibles ; aucun corrige officiel n'existe, toutes les cles sont a verifier contre le bareme du Board si on le trouve.

Questions 8 et 14 : le sujet imprime deux versions sous un meme numero (la version avec schema, puis 'OR' et une version sans schema). Les deux versions ont la meme lettre : Q8 C (structure 3 = glande surrenale, et option C Adrenal), Q14 A (structure 2 = cloison, et option A Septum). Ce sont donc des QCM a cle unique ; la version alternative est recopiee dans l'enonce avec ses options. Le 'OR' ne se code pas par une regle de choix (parmi / ou) : il n'y a ni section ni sous-question, et une regle n'aurait aucun effet sur la notation puisque la cle est la meme.

Questions 8 et 14 : schemas grossiers (photocopie). Q8 : la structure 3 est dessinee au sommet du rein, donc la glande surrenale ; 1 hypophyse, 2 thyroide, 4 gonade ; le pancreas est dessine sans etiquette. Q14 : la fleche 2 pointe la paroi centrale (cloison) ; la lecture du dessin est moins sure que celle de la version alternative, qui donne la meme cle A.

Question 30 : deux options sont defendables (D pere normal et mere porteuse, le cas usuel ; B pere hemophile et mere porteuse, possible si la fille 'normale' est porteuse). Convertie en question ouverte, reponse visee D.
Question 7 : cle D (electrochemical) ; 'Electrical' (C) est aussi employe dans certains manuels camerounais.
Question 12 : cle A ; l'option C (le diaphragme se relache) est vraie mais moins precise, car A dit comment le diaphragme bouge (vers le haut).
Question 13 : cle B (denatured) ; l'option C (inactivated by heat) est vraie mais B nomme le mecanisme.
Question 20 : cle B ; l'option A (empeche l'ecoulement de la lymphe dans differentes directions) dit presque la meme chose, B est la formulation exacte.
Question 26 : cle B (voix grave) ; la voix des filles change aussi legerement a la puberte, mais c'est le caractere propre aux garcons parmi les options.
Question 33 : cle A (1, 2 et 3) ; 'teach prisoners arts and craft' releve de la reinsertion, que le sujet semble compter comme une fonction de la prison.
Question 44 : cle A (cirrhose, consequence directe) ; le cancer du foie (D) est une complication plus tardive et a d'autres causes.
Question 50 : cle B (inconscient en premier) ; regle de premiers secours, les victimes qui crient ou appellent respirent et sont conscientes.

Fautes d'impression conservees : credit du schema Q14 'Roland Super' (ailleurs 'Soper'), Q14/Q15 sans point apres le numero 15, 'diarrhea', 'center', 'Pediatric', 'tape worm', Q38 'Chlorofluorocarbons', Q19 'a single breath', Q29 'the developing zygote'.

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 30. Cle visee D (pere normal, mere porteuse), mais B (pere hemophile, mere porteuse) est aussi possible si la fille normale est porteuse.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which characteristic do humans and birds have in common?
questions.corrige_markdown: Humans and birds are both warm-blooded (homeothermic): they keep a nearly constant internal body temperature whatever the temperature outside. A muscular diaphragm, diphyodont dentition (two sets of teeth, milk teeth then permanent teeth) and mammary glands are mammalian features: birds have no diaphragm, no teeth and no mammary glands. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Diffusion differs from active transport in that:
questions.corrige_markdown: Diffusion is passive: particles move from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration, that is down (along) the concentration gradient, using no energy. Active transport is the opposite: it moves substances against the gradient (low to high), it is selective and it uses energy from ATP, which is what options A, B and C describe. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: It occurs against a concentration gradient
It involves the use of ATP
It occurs along a concentration gradient.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a difference between a typical plant cell and a typical animal cell:
questions.corrige_markdown: Only plant cells have a cellulose cell wall outside the cell membrane; animal cells have no cell wall. The other options are all reversed: plant cells have chloroplasts (A), store starch while animal cells store glycogen (C), and a mature plant cell has one large central vacuole while animal cells have small vacuoles (D). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Plant cell: lacks chloroplasts; animal cell: has chloroplasts
Plant cell: has a cellulose cell wall; animal cell: lacks a cellulose cell wall
Plant cell: contains glycogen granules; animal cell: contains starch granules
Plant cell: has many small vacuoles; animal cell: has a large central vacuole.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a connective tissue?
questions.corrige_markdown: Connective tissues join, support or transport and have cells scattered in a matrix: blood is a fluid connective tissue (cells in the plasma matrix). Skeletal and smooth muscle are muscle tissues and the neurone is nervous tissue. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What type of joint is found between the femur and tibia of the leg?
questions.corrige_markdown: The knee joint, between the femur and the tibia, lets the leg bend and straighten in one plane only, like a door: it is a hinge joint. Ball-and-socket joints are at the hip and shoulder, a pivot joint is at the top of the neck and gliding joints are between the wrist bones. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What happens when the hand is pricked with a needle?
questions.corrige_markdown: Pricking the hand starts a reflex action: the arm is pulled away from the needle by bending (flexing) the elbow. The biceps, the flexor, contracts and its antagonist, the triceps, relaxes. The triceps contracting would straighten the arm, and the brachialis is also a flexor, so it would contract, not relax. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the nature of a nerve impulse?
questions.corrige_markdown: A nerve impulse is a wave of change in the electrical potential of the neurone membrane (action potential) caused by the movement of sodium and potassium ions across it: it is electrical in effect but chemical in origin, so it is described as electrochemical. Only the transmission across a synapse is purely chemical (neurotransmitters). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
![fig-1](gce-ol-human-biology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

The diagram below shows the main endocrine glands in the human body.

Which numbered structure secretes a hormone that prepares the body to cope with any threatening situation?

**OR** (alternative version printed under the same number)

Which endocrine gland secretes a hormone that prepares the body to cope with any threatening situation?

*Options of the alternative version:* A. Gonad   B. Pituitary   C. Adrenal   D. Thyroid.
questions.corrige_markdown: The hormone that prepares the body for danger (fight or flight) is adrenaline, secreted by the adrenal glands, which sit on top of the kidneys. In the diagram this is structure 3 (1 is the pituitary in the head, 2 the thyroid in the neck and 4 a gonad), so the answer is C. In the alternative version without the diagram the gland is the adrenal gland, which is also option C, so both versions have the same key. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Under which condition will protein digestion take place in the stomach?
questions.corrige_markdown: In the stomach the enzyme pepsin digests proteins into peptides. Pepsin works best at about pH 2, which the hydrochloric acid of the gastric juice provides, so digestion takes place in acidic conditions. Alkaline conditions suit the enzymes of the small intestine, such as trypsin. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the immediate by-product of anaerobic respiration in skeletal muscle tissue?
questions.corrige_markdown: When a muscle works hard and oxygen is short, glucose is broken down incompletely: glucose gives lactic acid and a little energy. Lactic acid builds up and causes fatigue and cramps. Ethanol and carbon dioxide are the products of anaerobic respiration in yeast, a common wrong choice, and oxygen is used up, not produced. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select a mineral element that influences the proper growth of teeth:
questions.corrige_markdown: Calcium (with phosphorus and vitamin D) is needed to build strong bones and to harden the enamel and dentine of the teeth. Iron is needed for haemoglobin, so a lack of it causes anaemia. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What happens during exhalation in humans?
questions.corrige_markdown: During exhalation the external intercostal muscles relax so the ribs move down and in, and the diaphragm relaxes and returns to its dome shape, moving upwards. The chest volume decreases, the pressure inside rises and air is pushed out. Option B describes inhalation. Option C is true but less complete since it does not say how the diaphragm moves, and a diaphragm does not move 'outwards' (D). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The intercostal muscles relax and the diaphragm moves upwards
The intercostal muscles contract and the diaphragm flattens
The intercostal muscles relax and the diaphragm relaxes
The intercostal muscles relax and the diaphragm moves outwards.

questions.enonce_markdown: A solution containing salivary amylase was heated to a temperature of 95°C and then added to a solution of cooked starch. The reason why this solution will test negative for reducing sugar is:
questions.corrige_markdown: An enzyme is a protein. At 95°C its three-dimensional shape is destroyed (it is denatured), so the active site no longer fits the starch and no starch is broken down to maltose, a reducing sugar. The Benedict's test therefore stays blue (negative). Heat does not activate the enzyme (D), and the denaturation is permanent, so waiting longer would not help (A). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The time was too short for salivary amylase to act on cooked starch
Salivary amylase has been denatured by heat
Salivary amylase was inactivated by heat
The salivary amylase was activated by heat.

questions.enonce_markdown:
![fig-2](gce-ol-human-biology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

The diagram below is that of the longitudinal section through the human heart. (Courtesy of Roland Super, Human Biology Study Guide)

Identify the part numbered 2:

**OR** (alternative version printed under the same number)

Which structure in the human heart separates the left and right sides?

*Options of the alternative version:* A. Septum   B. Papillary muscle   C. Left ventricle   D. Right ventricle.
questions.corrige_markdown: The arrow numbered 2 points to the thick muscular wall running down the middle of the heart: this is the septum, which separates the right side of the heart from the left side and keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood apart. In the alternative version the structure that separates the two sides is also the septum (option A), so both versions have the same key. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The part of the human brain which controls homeostasis is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The hypothalamus monitors the temperature, water content and sugar level of the blood and sends messages to the pituitary gland and other organs to correct them, so it is the control centre of homeostasis. The medulla oblongata controls the heartbeat and breathing, and the cerebellum controls balance and coordination of movement. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the role played by blood in the defence of the body against infection:
questions.corrige_markdown: Blood defends the body through its white blood cells: lymphocytes produce antibodies that attack pathogens, and phagocytes engulf them. The other options are real functions of blood (heat distribution, transport of urea) or of other organs, but none of them is a defence against infection. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Transports heat from muscles and liver to the rest of the body
Controls the water and nutrient levels in the body
Transports nitrogenous wastes to excretory organs.

questions.enonce_markdown: In the renal system, which structure stores urine?
questions.corrige_markdown: The kidneys make urine, the ureters carry it down, the bladder stores it until it is released, and the urethra carries it out of the body. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The testicles of human males are suspended in the scrotum because:
questions.corrige_markdown: Sperm are produced best at about 2 to 3°C below the normal body temperature of 37°C. Hanging outside the abdomen in the scrotum keeps the testes slightly cooler, which gives the right temperature for sperm production. Option C is the opposite of the truth. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: This provides the right temperature for sperm production
It is easier for the body to expel sperm during ejaculation
The optimum temperature for sperm production is higher than the normal body temperature
There is not enough space in the pelvic area for the testicles to be housed internally.

questions.enonce_markdown: The maximum volume of air that can be moved in and out of the lungs during a single breath is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Vital capacity is the largest volume of air that can be breathed out after the deepest possible breath in (tidal volume plus inspiratory and expiratory reserve volumes). Tidal volume is only the air moved in ordinary quiet breathing, and total lung capacity also includes the residual air that always stays in the lungs. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the role of valves in lymphatics?
questions.corrige_markdown: Lymph vessels, like veins, contain valves. Lymph is pushed along by the squeezing of the surrounding muscles, and the valves stop it from flowing backwards, so it moves only towards the heart. Option D is the opposite of their role, and the valves do not deal with blood (C). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Prevent the flow of lymph in different directions
Prevent the back flow of blood
Prevent the flow of lymph from tissues to the heart.

questions.enonce_markdown: Why is the second pregnancy of a Rh-negative mother bearing a Rh-positive foetus dangerous?
questions.corrige_markdown: During the first birth some Rh-positive blood of the baby mixes with the mother's blood, and her immune system makes anti-rhesus antibodies. In a second pregnancy with an Rh-positive foetus these antibodies cross the placenta and destroy the red blood cells of the foetus (haemolytic disease), which may kill the foetus in the womb. The mother makes more antibodies, not fewer (A), and the baby is not deformed (C). **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The mother develops less anti-rhesus antibodies
The foetus may die in the womb.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which hormone is correctly paired with its function?
questions.corrige_markdown: Oxytocin, released by the pituitary gland, makes the muscles of the breasts contract to eject milk (it also causes contractions of the uterus at birth). Thyroxine controls the metabolic rate (A), antidiuretic hormone stimulates the reabsorption of water in the kidney, not sodium ions (B), and milk production is stimulated by prolactin, not progesterone (D). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Antidiuretic hormone: stimulates the reabsorption of sodium ions
Oxytocin: stimulates milk ejection from the breasts
Progesterone: stimulates the breasts to produce milk.

questions.enonce_markdown: How is the foetus protected by the placenta?
questions.corrige_markdown: The placenta acts as a barrier: it stops many pathogens and harmful substances in the mother's blood from reaching the foetus. Supplying oxygen and nutrients and producing hormones such as human chorionic gonadotrophin are functions of the placenta, but they feed and support the foetus rather than protect it. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: It allows the foetus to get enough oxygen
It allows the foetus to get enough nutrients
It prevents some pathogens getting to the foetus

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the phenotype of an organism?
questions.corrige_markdown: The phenotype is the observable characteristic of an organism (for example tall, blood group A, brown eyes), produced by its genotype and the environment. The allele combination, and the homozygous or heterozygous state, describe the genotype. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The allele combination in an organism
The visible traits of an organism
The homozygous state of an organism
The heterozygous state of an organism.

questions.enonce_markdown: The digestive disorder, diarrhea is characterized by:
questions.corrige_markdown: Diarrhoea is the passing of frequent, loose and watery stools because the large intestine does not absorb enough water. Bloody stools are typical of dysentery, and constipation is the opposite disorder, with hard and infrequent stools. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select a secondary sexual characteristic common to boys only:
questions.corrige_markdown: At puberty testosterone makes the larynx of boys grow, so their voice breaks and becomes deep and coarse. Widened hips and the development of mammary glands occur in girls, and pubic hair grows in both boys and girls. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How does the skin perceive changes in the environment?
questions.corrige_markdown: The skin contains many sensory receptors in the dermis (for touch, pressure, pain, heat and cold) that detect stimuli and send impulses to the brain. The other options are real functions of the skin, protection, lubrication and temperature regulation, but they are not about sensing the environment. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Has many receptors sensitive to stimuli
Has the cornified layer which prevents the entry of pathogens
Has the dermis containing sebaceous gland that secretes sebum
Has many sweat glands that regulates body temperature.

questions.enonce_markdown: In the mammalian ear, what is the function of the eustachian tube?
questions.corrige_markdown: The eustachian tube joins the middle ear to the throat. It lets air in or out so that the air pressure in the middle ear equals the pressure outside, on the other side of the ear drum, so the ear drum can vibrate freely. Vibrations are carried to the cochlea by the ossicles, which also magnify them. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It equalizes the air pressure between the oval window and the round window
It equalizes the air pressure on either side of the ear drum
It transmits vibrations to the cochlea
It magnifies the vibrations of the ear ossicles.

questions.enonce_markdown: The sinking and attachment of the developing zygote into the thickened uterine wall is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: After fertilisation the zygote divides into a ball of cells that reaches the uterus and sinks into its thickened lining about 7 days later: this is implantation. Fertilisation is the fusion of sperm and egg, ovulation is the release of the egg, and gestation is the whole period of development in the womb. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Haemophilia is a sex-linked recessive trait in humans. What would be the possible phenotypes of the parents of a haemophiliac son and a normal daughter?

*Options as printed:* A) Father: Carrier; Mother: Normal   B) Father: Haemophiliac; Mother: Carrier   C) Father: Carrier; Mother: Haemophiliac   D) Father: Normal; Mother: Carrier.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Haemophilia is carried on the X chromosome (Xh = haemophilia allele, XH = normal allele). The haemophiliac son XhY got his Y from the father and his Xh from the mother, so the mother carries the allele: she is a carrier (XHXh). A normal father (XHY) crossed with a carrier mother gives sons XHY (normal) or XhY (haemophiliac) and daughters XHXH or XHXh (all normal), which fits the family described. A man cannot be a carrier (A and C), and a mother who is not a carrier cannot have a haemophiliac son (A). A haemophiliac father with a carrier mother (B) would also fit if the normal daughter is a carrier, which is why the intended answer is the usual case, normal father and carrier mother.

**Intended answer: D (Father: Normal; Mother: Carrier).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Bacterial diseases include:

1) Poliomyelitis
2) Typhoid
3) Tuberculosis.
questions.corrige_markdown: Poliomyelitis is caused by a virus (statement 1 is wrong). Typhoid fever is caused by the bacterium *Salmonella typhi* and tuberculosis by *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*, so statements 2 and 3 are correct. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
How is a leaf adapted to carry out photosynthesis?

1) It has a thin upper epidermis
2) It has many chloroplasts
3) It has many stomata on its upper surface.
questions.corrige_markdown: A thin, transparent upper epidermis lets light reach the palisade cells (1 is correct), and the many chloroplasts in these cells trap the light (2 is correct). Most stomata are on the lower surface, where it is cooler and less water is lost, so statement 3 is wrong. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
What are the functions of a prison?

1) Punish criminals
2) Reform criminals
3) Teach prisoners arts and craft.
questions.corrige_markdown: A prison is a social institution that punishes wrongdoers by taking away their freedom (1), reforms them so that they can return to society as good citizens (2), and trains them in skills such as arts and crafts so that they can earn a living after release (3). All three statements are correct. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is/are fungal diseases?

1) Ringworm
2) Athlete's foot
3) Thrush.
questions.corrige_markdown: Ringworm and athlete's foot are skin infections caused by fungi (moulds that grow on the skin), and thrush is caused by the yeast *Candida albicans*. All three are fungal diseases. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Foods that contain much water and organic matter and are easily attacked by bacteria are called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Foods rich in water and organic matter, such as milk, meat, fish and fresh vegetables, are quickly spoiled by bacteria: they are perishable foods. Non-perishable foods, such as dry grains, keep for a long time. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A material that is obtained from tiny threads spun by the larvae of a worm is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Silk is a natural animal fibre: the larva (caterpillar) of the silkworm moth spins a cocoon of fine threads, which are unwound and spun into silk. Cotton and linen are plant fibres (from the cotton boll and the flax stem) and nylon is a synthetic fibre. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
In the food chain below, which organism is the secondary consumer?

Orange tree → Grasshopper → Lizard → Hawk
questions.corrige_markdown: The orange tree is the producer, the grasshopper eats the plant and is the primary consumer, the lizard eats the grasshopper and is therefore the secondary consumer, and the hawk is the tertiary consumer. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a common air pollutant?
questions.corrige_markdown: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) from refrigerators and aerosol sprays are air pollutants that destroy the ozone layer. Nitrogen is a normal gas of the air (78%), raw sewage pollutes water and mercury mostly pollutes water and soil. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: HIV/AIDS could be transmitted by?
questions.corrige_markdown: HIV passes through body fluids such as blood, semen, vaginal fluid and breast milk. Transfusion of contaminated blood puts the virus directly into the blood. Screened blood has been tested and is safe, and handshaking or sharing plates does not transmit the virus. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Eating using the same plates with a patient.

questions.enonce_markdown: Rising damp in walls of houses is due to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Rising damp is water from the ground that creeps up the walls by capillary action. It happens when the wall has no damp-proof course (a waterproof layer such as plastic sheeting or bitumen laid in the wall near the ground). Defective roofing and broken gutters let water in from above, not from the ground. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a symptom of malaria?
questions.corrige_markdown: Malaria is caused by *Plasmodium*, which destroys red blood cells. The symptoms are fever with shivering and sweating, headache, and general body weakness because of the anaemia. Madness and shouting are not symptoms of malaria. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the micro-organism responsible for converting nitrites to nitrates in the nitrogen cycle:
questions.corrige_markdown: Nitrifying bacteria (*Nitrosomonas* then *Nitrobacter*) change ammonium compounds into nitrites and then nitrites into nitrates, which plants can absorb. Nitrogen-fixing bacteria change nitrogen gas to nitrogen compounds, denitrifying bacteria change nitrates back to nitrogen gas, and decay bacteria release ammonia from dead matter. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A center that treats patients with mental disorder is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: A psychiatric centre (hospital) treats people with mental disorders. Paediatric care is for children, obstetric care is for pregnant women and childbirth, and a polyclinic treats many kinds of ordinary illnesses. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose a disease which is a direct consequence of too much alcohol consumption:
questions.corrige_markdown: The liver breaks down alcohol, and too much alcohol over a long time destroys liver cells which are replaced by scar tissue: this is cirrhosis of the liver. Pneumonia is an infection and emphysema is mostly caused by smoking. Liver cancer has several causes and is a later complication rather than the direct effect. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the gas in the atmosphere which brings about global warming:
questions.corrige_markdown: Carbon dioxide, released by burning fuels and by deforestation, is a greenhouse gas: it traps heat in the atmosphere and raises the temperature of the Earth. Oxygen, hydrogen and helium are not greenhouse gases. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A break in a bone is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A broken bone is a fracture. A sprain is the tearing of a ligament, a dislocation is a bone pulled out of its joint, and a bruise is bleeding under the skin. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The solid wastes from homes and industries are called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Garbage (refuse) is the solid waste from homes and industries. Sewage and sludge are liquid or semi-liquid wastes from toilets and sewage plants, and effluent is liquid waste from factories. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What stage in the life cycle of the pork tape worm (*Taenia solium*) is found in the muscle of a pig?
questions.corrige_markdown: The pig swallows eggs, they hatch into oncospheres in its gut, the oncospheres bore into the blood and settle in the muscles where each forms a bladderworm (cysticercus). People get the tapeworm by eating undercooked pork containing bladderworms. The proglottides are the segments of the adult worm in the human intestine. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Infections acquired while in the hospital are known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: An infection caught in a hospital by a patient being treated for something else is a nosocomial (hospital-acquired) infection. The other terms describe how or whether a disease spreads, not where it was caught. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: At the scene of a motor accident where several persons have been injured, who is the person to be attended to first?
questions.corrige_markdown: In first aid the priority is the casualty in the greatest danger. A person who is unconscious cannot call out and may have a blocked airway or be bleeding, so he or she can die in a few minutes without help. Those who are crying or calling for help are conscious and breathing, so they can wait a little longer. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Someone who is crying for help
Someone who is calling for help
